name: Posterior (dorsal) horn
summary: The sensory part of the spinal gray matter, where dorsal root fibers end and are processed before ascending. Its laminae are functionally stacked: the marginal zone (lamina I) and substantia gelatinosa (lamina II) receive pain and temperature fibers and are the site of opioid and gate-control modulation, the nucleus proprius (laminae III–V) handles touch and gives rise to the spinothalamic tract, and Clarke's column (lamina VII, C8–L3) sends proprioception to the cerebellum. Central sensitization here underlies chronic pain, and its destruction by a syrinx produces the dissociated sensory loss of the central cord syndrome.

anatomy.location: Posterior part of the gray matter on each side, reaching toward the posterolateral sulcus where the dorsal rootlets enter; capped by the substantia gelatinosa and Lissauer's tract.

subdivisions.name: Lamina I (marginal zone) and lamina II (substantia gelatinosa)
subdivisions.note: nociceptive and thermal input; enkephalinergic interneurons

subdivisions.name: Laminae III–IV (nucleus proprius)
subdivisions.note: tactile input; origin of spinothalamic and spinoreticular fibers

subdivisions.name: Lamina V
subdivisions.note: wide dynamic range neurons, visceral convergence (referred pain)

function: First relay and modulation of pain, temperature and crude touch; segmental reflexes; origin of the spinothalamic and spinocerebellar tracts.

bestView.label: posterior gray horns of the upper cervical cord

imaging.normalAppearance: The posterior limbs of the gray butterfly on high-resolution axial T2; a syrinx expands the central gray and obliterates them.

pathology.finding: Central cavity expanding into the posterior horns and crossing spinothalamic fibers.

pathology.pathology: Dorsal horn involvement in herpes zoster
pathology.finding: Rarely, T2 hyperintensity of the dorsal horn and root entry zone with segmental pain.

lesionEffects.deficit: Segmental loss of pain and temperature with preserved touch and proprioception
lesionEffects.mechanism: Substantia gelatinosa and nucleus proprius before the fibers cross
Central sensitization of dorsal horn neurons

examination: Pin-prick and temperature versus light touch in the affected dermatomes
pearls: Dissociated segmental sensory loss (pain gone, touch kept) is the dorsal horn or the crossing fibers in front of it: think syrinx
Referred visceral pain is lamina V convergence
